notes:
ACCESS: no bot wall. probe.fetch() returned HTTP 200 on the first try for every URL; no 403, no challenge, no membership gate. ROBOTS (www.quince.com/robots.txt, fetched first, HTTP 200, 2333 bytes): NO Claude opt-out. The generic group is 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' with Disallow only on /account/*, /accounts/*, /log-in*, /sign-up*, /tracking*, /checkout/thank-you*, /p/* and /partner/*. There IS a named Anthropic group - 'User-agent: Claude-SearchBot' - but it carries the SAME eight path Disallows and NOT 'Disallow: /', so it is not an opt-out; it does not cover /shop/* and it does not cover the sitemaps. ClaudeBot / anthropic-ai / Claude-Web are not named at all, so the '*' group governs us either way. Note the site disallows /*?*sortBy=, /*?*utm_ etc ONLY inside the 'User-agent: Googlebot' group; I still used no sort, facet, utm or search URL anywhere. No disallowed path was requested. No Crawl-delay declared; probe.py's 2s/host gap was used throughout. api.onequince.com (the regional API host named in the Next.js payload) was deliberately NEVER contacted - it is a separate host that would need its own robots check, and all counts came from the page's own server-rendered payload instead.
TREE: taken from the site's OWN mega-menu, not guessed. Homepage __NEXT_DATA__ -> props.pageProps.siteData.siteData.menuPrimary[6] ('Home') -> submenuColumnTwo -> header 'Bath', which lists exactly four entries: Shop All (/shop/home/all-bath), Bath Towels & Bundles, Bath Mats, Robes & Accessories. The mega-menu TRUNCATES (BATCH_BRIEF s5): the category sitemap recovers two further real children of all-bath that appear in no menu - Shower Curtains and Baby & Kids Towels - and, critically, a seventh node the menu never shows: BATHROOM ACCESSORIES. Sitemap route: /sitemap.xml -> /sitemap_us.xml -> sitemap_shop.xml (537 locs) + sitemap_subcollections.xml (1174) + sitemap_misc.xml (94), 1800 URLs total. sitemap_subcollections.xml declares exactly six children of /shop/home/all-bath/: baby-kids-towels, bath-mats, bath-towels-bundles, bathroom-accessories, luxury-robes, shower-curtains. Each was fetched and its rel=canonical followed; four of the six canonicalise away from the /all-bath/ form (blind spot (a)) and the canonical form is what is recorded. All 319 /shop/home/* URLs were listed and swept for soap|toilet|faucet|tap|sink|vanit|tub|hardware|hook|shelf|caddy|dispenser|organiz|tray|basket|hamper|brush|tooth|bidet|toiletr - the only hits were curtain rods-hardware (window curtains), consoles-bookshelves (Furniture, already extracted), storage-organization, and travel toiletry bags (luggage). There is NO sanitaryware, NO tap/faucet, NO shower fitting, NO bath, NO toilet, NO vanity unit and NO bathroom mirror anywhere in the taxonomy - Quince is a DTC soft-goods brand and its Bath department is almost entirely Textile.
ROWS: exactly one Bathroom leaf. 'Bathroom Accessories' (H1 'Bathroom Accessories', canonical https://www.quince.com/shop/home/bathroom-accessories) holds the 'Handwoven Rattan Bathroom Accessories Set' and the 'Handwoven Rattan Hamper' - a bathroom accessory set is Bathroom under rule 13, and the node's own name and its parentage under all-bath settle the hierarchy question (rule 2: website category hierarchy). The alias /shop/home/all-bath/bathroom-accessories rel=canonicals onto the recorded URL and is therefore ONE record under rule 28, not two.
QTY: recorded 2 = DISTINCT PRODUCTS, enumerated to exhaustion. Basis and proof: the PLP is server-rendered into __NEXT_DATA__; the widget of type PRODUCT_LIST carries pagination {limit:30, hasMore:false, total:N} and one PRODUCT_CARD child per card, and for this node hasMore is false, so the payload IS the whole collection - this is enumeration to exhaustion, not a reported total. WHY NOT THE RENDERED FIGURE: Quince's own rendered 'N items' (data-testid=collection-product-count), its filterSortData.total, its pagination.total and its JSON-LD numberOfItems all agree with each other on any single fetch, but they count COLOURWAY CARDS, not products, AND they are UNSTABLE - ten fetches of this exact URL across the session returned 3,3,3,3,3,4,4,4,4 (one fetch rendered no count element at all). The 3-variant suppresses one colourway card of the hamper; the 4-variant shows the full 2 products x 2 colourways (Natural / White Wash) grid. The DISTINCT product set was identical in all ten fetches: ids 8669 and 8670. This is the Sostrene Grene instability trap (BATCH_BRIEF s3) - an unstable figure is not an 'exact figure shown on the listing page' under rule 26, so the reproducible distinct-product count is recorded and the card figures are disclosed here in full. Same instability was proved on Bath Mats (8 vs 9 cards, 3 distinct in every fetch).
VERIFICATION: counts discriminate (2 / 3 / 5 / 12 / 27 / 94 across the nodes examined - no site-wide constant). Every H1 was checked against the node requested and matched. Pagination arithmetic was NOT used anywhere: ?page=2 and ?cursor=30 on /shop/home/all-bath both re-serve page 1 with an identical first-three product sequence (the IKEA trap, confirmed here), so pagination was never multiplied. JSON-LD was checked and REJECTED as a source: all-bath's ItemList claims numberOfItems 134 while emitting only 20 itemListElement entries.
DEDUP (OPTION 1, URL-exact index): already_extracted() was run on all 21 candidate/alias/canonical URLs touched. ZERO hits. quince.com appears in the index only via Furniture.xlsx, with 12 furniture nodes (living-room, dining-room, bedroom, outdoor) - none of them bathroom, none of them a vanity, and no bath vanity or bathroom cabinet exists on this site to be deduped. Blind spots worked: (a) every rel=canonical target was index-checked as well as the fetched URL; (b)/(c) locale - the sitemap index exposes /ca/, /fr-ca/ and /uk/ storefronts on the same host, but this company is USA and both prior workbooks recorded Quince under the bare www.quince.com/shop/ US form, so there is no locale-alias miss; (d) the /all-bath/ duplicate path is collapsed to the canonical, one record.
EXCLUDED and why: Bath Towels & Bundles, Bath Mats, Robes & Accessories, Shower Curtains and Baby & Kids Towels -> Textile (rules 15/16/20), all five in review[] with URLs and qty. Home Decor > Mirrors -> not recorded: 5 general decorative wall mirrors under Home Decor, no bathroom/vanity/LED mirror exists (rule 11 judged on primary type, and BATCH_BRIEF s6's warning that 'mirror' is a false-positive magnet applies). Home Decor > Storage & Organization -> withheld as general Storage AND as a proven overlap: it contains both products of the recorded Bathroom Accessories leaf, so recording it too would double-count them. Shop All / all-bath -> rule 25 + rule 24. No empty nodes were found in the Bath tree; /shop/home/living-room-decor/mirrors resolves but renders no grid and is noted as an empty alias in review.
